claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you some questions.

Let me start with the basics:

**Do you have any children you're responsible for?** If yes, please tell me:
- How many children you have
- Their names (or you can use Child 1, Child 2, etc. if you prefer)
- Their ages

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello! Yes, I'd like to find out if I can claim Child Benefit. I have one child - Alex, who's 16 years old.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! I have a few questions about Alex to help determine your eligibility.

**Is Alex currently in approved education or training?** (For example, studying at school, college, or in an approved training program)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, Alex is still in education - doing A-levels at sixth form college.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
That's helpful, thank you. Now I need to understand a bit more about your living situation and residence status.

**Do you currently live in the UK, and does Alex live with you?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK and Alex lives at home with me.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Excellent. Now I need to check your immigration and residence status:

**Are you a British citizen, or do you have settled status, pre-settled status, or another immigration status in the UK?**

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for providing that information. I have just a couple more questions to complete the assessment:

**Is anyone else currently claiming Child Benefit for Alex?** (For example, Alex's other parent or another family member)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, nobody else is claiming Child Benefit for Alex.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect. One final question:

**Has Alex started any paid work for 24 hours or more per week, or is Alex claiming any benefits in their own right** (such as Employment and Support Allowance or Universal Credit)?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, Alex doesn't work that much and isn't claiming any benefits themselves.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Good news! **You are ELIGIBLE for Child Benefit for Alex.**

Here's why:

✓ You are a British citizen living in the UK  
✓ Alex lives with you, establishing that you're responsible for them  
✓ Although Alex is 16, you still qualify because Alex is in approved education (A-levels at sixth form college). Child Benefit can continue for children under 20 who stay in approved education or training  
✓ Alex is not working 24+ hours per week  
✓ Alex is not claiming benefits independently  
✓ Nobody else is claiming Child Benefit for Alex  

You meet all the eligibility requirements and should be able to successfully apply for Child Benefit.

**Important note:** If you or your partner have an individual income over £60,000, you may need to pay the High Income Child Benefit tax charge. You can still claim Child Benefit, but you might have to pay back some or all of it through the tax system.

Would you like any further information about claiming Child Benefit?
